question: The first modern Olympic Games are held in Athens, Greece.
LEGO releases its very first plastic brick.
The board game Monopoly is first published by Parker Brothers.
Serena Williams wins her first Grand Slam singles title at the US Open.
Nintendo releases the Game Boy in Japan.
The Rubik’s Cube is invented by Ernő Rubik in Hungary.
Tiger Woods becomes the youngest golfer to win the Masters Tournament.
Gary Gygax and Dave Arneson publishes the first edition of Dungeons & Dragons.
The first ever FIFA World Cup is held in Uruguay.
The popular Tamagotchi virtual pets are released in Japan.
Scrabble is released in Sweden, though renamed as Alfapet.
Cassius Clay changes his name to Muhammad Ali.
The FIFA World cup is hosted in the US, and Sweden is awarded bronze.
Parasite wins an Oscar for Best Picture.
At the Hollywood Roosevelt Hotel, the Academy Awards ceremony is held for the first time.
The Jazz Singer, the first feature-length film with synchronized dialogue, is released.
Netflix launches its streaming service, changing how movies are distributed and watched.
Disney acquires Pixar, marking a major shift in the animation industry.
The record company Decca turns down the offer to sign a record deal with the Beatles.
The skit show Saturday Night Live premieres on american television.
Johnny Depp has his feature film debut with the cult horror classic Nightmare on Elm Street.
Sweden becomes the first country in the world with a state mandated film censorship.
The two-venue benefit concert and music-based fundraising initiative Live Aid aired around the world.
The iconic Marilyn Monroe passes away.
Both Janis Joplin and Jimi Hendrix passes away.
Beavis and Butt-head premieres on MTV.
The literary adventures of Robin Hood is adapted to film for the very first time.
Video Killed the Radio Star becomes the first music video to air on MTV.

question: The artist Vincent van Gogh slices off his ear.
Dante begins his descent into hell and purgatory.
The artist Edvard Munch finishes “The Scream”, which becomes one of his most prolific paintings.
Ian Fleming writes the first book about international spy James Bond.
Agatha Christie has her debut.
Vlad III, famous for being the inspiration for Dracula, dies.
Leonardo da Vinci finishes The Mona Lisa.
The Brothers Grimm publish a collection of their fairy tales for the first time.
The Murders in the Rue Morgue by Edgar Allan Poe, a predecessor to the detective fiction genre, was released.
The first issue of the American fashion magazine Vogue is published.
George Orwell releases his dystopian novel and cautionary tale Nineteen Eighty-Four.
Tolkien's book about Bilbo, The Hobbit, is published in England.
Oscar Wilde is sentenced to two years in prison for “gross indecency”.
Dr. Christiaan Barnard performs the first successful heart transplant.
The Hubble Space Telescope is successfully launched into orbit.
Marie Curie is awarded the Nobel Prize in Chemistry following her discovery of radium and polonium.
The first website goes live on the World Wide Web.
Dolly the sheep is born, making her the first mammal to be cloned from an adult somatic cell.
Isaac Newton publishes Philosophiæ Naturalis Principia Mathematica, laying the groundwork for classical mechanics.
An accident in Alexander Fleming’s lab causes him to discover penicillin.
Egas Moniz, who introduced the world to the lobotomy, is awarded the Nobel Prize in Medicine.
Apple introduces the first iPhone.
Galileo Galilei turns his telescope to the night sky for the first time and observes Jupiter’s moons.
Russia beats USA to space by successfully launching their satellite Sputnik.
Douglas Engelbart proudly presents his new invention; the computer mouse.
Mobira Talkman, the clunky predecessor to the modern mobile phone, is launched by Nokia.
A norwegian carpenter invents the cheese slicer (aka osthyvel).
The first well-documented caesarean section was performed on a live woman.
William Shakespeare gets married to Anne Hathaway.
Two years after disappearing during a solo flight across the Pacific Ocean, Amelia Earhart is declared dead.
Hostages during a bank robbery start sympathizing with their captor Janne Olsson, generating the term “Stockholm Syndrome”.
Nelson Mandela is freed from prison after 27 years.
Marie Antoinette marries Ludvig XVI.
John Lennon is fatally shot outside of his home by Mark Chapman.
Six-year-old Mozart performs for the Austrian Emperor.
Famed explorer Marco Polo dies.
Jack the Ripper murders at least five women.
Divorce becomes legal in Italy.
The construction of the Berlin wall begins.
Pompei is buried as a result of the volcano Vesuvius erupting.
The beginning of the Islamic Calendar.
The meaning behind the abbreviation “Y2K”.
The first documented sighting of the Loch Ness Monster.
The first gas station in the US is built.
The video hosting website Youtube is launched.
The Nordics’ first university is founded in Uppsala.
The No. 4 reactor of the Chernobyl Nuclear Power Plant explodes.
Alcohol is no longer illegal to imbibe or sell, as the prohibition era in the US finally ends.
